I went to primary school, so I can read what is written on a seed packet or fertilizer bag, but I learned how to farm from watching my mother and my neighbors. This plot is only a quarter hectare and it is rented, so I do not want to spend a lot of money on inputs that I cannot take with me if the landlord changes his mind. Last season I put manure from my cows on this piece and used seed I kept from the previous harvest, and the maize gave us enough to eat for several months. I will do the same this year — manure, my own seed, and hand weeding with my children. I wanted to buy a small amount of urea, but by the time I had the cash in hand, the agro-dealer in town had already sold his stock, and one full bag is too much money for this small plot anyway. We will work the land ourselves with hand hoes; it will take us about twenty days spread from planting to when we finish shelling the cobs.
